title: SLO/SLI declaration for per-endpoint and variant prioritization with failover & circuit hysteresis
creator: Grace Kim
description: Purpose: Produce a canonical SLO/SLI declaration and operational policy that ties per-endpoint request quality, latency, and availability SLIs to automated error-budgeting, prioritized failover between regions and model variants, and hysteresis-aware circuit breaker thresholds. Scope includes: 1) canonical SLI definitions for text-generation and chat endpoints (p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latency SLI, availability by status codes, response-quality SLI for promptsets), 2) per-model-variant and per-route SLO templates, 3) error budget accounting (burn, crediting, escrow, borrowing rules), 4) circuit breaker thresholds with hysteresis and cooldown tied to SLO burn rates, 5) prioritized load-shedding rules for graceful degradation across Dedicated/Hosted/Private deployments, and 6) integration points for KV-cache impact and session-affinity on SLI attribution.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical SLI spec doc exists that defines metrics, collection windows, and calculation method for p50/p95/p99 latency, availability (5xx/4xx accounting rules), and response-quality (promptset-based regression metrics).
Per-endpoint SLO templates (P0/P1/P2 tiers) that can be applied to routes and model variants via the deployment manifest.
An error-budget policy that defines: burn rate calculation, credit/escrow mechanics for canaries, borrowing rules (time-limited), and emergency top-ups for on-call.
Circuit breaker recipes: threshold formula tied to 5m/1h burn rates, hysteresis (min-open, backoff multiplier), and automated fallback to pre-defined variant tiers.
Failover playbook that shows multi-region routing order, warm-standby requirements, KV-cache rehydration expectations, and steps for manual intervention.
A simulation run (load tests + synthetic errors) demonstrating expected behavior of load-shedding and circuit breakers under three failure scenarios with dashboards capturing SLI burn & recovery.
Guardrail automation: rollout gating based on SLO gates (canary fails to stop), and CLI/Console ops to adjust per-tenant priority slices.
work_items: Draft SLI calculation formulas and edge-case rules for partial responses and streaming cancellations.
Define variant priority bands (gold/silver/bronze) and mapping to circuit-breaker fallback actions.
Design error-budget ledger schema for cross-region borrow/repay operations and retention of burn history.
Prototype automation to convert SLO templates into runtime rules consumed by the routing layer.
Add KV-cache influence factor to SLI attribution rules and create example annotations for session-aware endpoints.
Create dashboards and synthetic test harness for the simulation scenarios.
decisions: Adopt percentile-based latency SLIs (p95 as primary SLO) but publish p50/p99 for signal richness.
Treat streaming partial responses as degraded quality and map to a quality SLI with a weighted penalty per missing token range.
Error budget borrowing allowed between temporal windows for canaries only, capped at 10% of target and must be repaid within 24h or triggers rollback.

Circuit breakers will use a burn-rate-aware threshold: if 15min burn > 3x target or 1h burn > 1.5x target, open breaker for variant and route. Hysteresis will require 2 consecutive cool windows before close.
notes: Trade-off: aggressive load-shedding preserves global availability but risks per-tenant quality regressions. We'll expose priority slices to customers to opt into degraded modes.
KV-cache plays a large role in tail latency; we add a cache-hit annotation to SLI samples and will track hit-rate-adjusted SLO projections.
Operational complexity increases with per-variant SLOs; initial rollout will default to per-route SLOs with opt-in per-variant tuning.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives from transient noisy metrics cause unnecessary failovers. Mitigation: require multi-window confirmation and correlate with infra signals before automatic region failover.
Risk: Error-budget borrowing used repeatedly degrades long-term quality. Mitigation: telemetry alert if borrow frequency > 2/month per route and enforce cooling period.
